certainty.note: Coastal forts, river posts and prazos; no frontier is described on the pages opened.

The Anglo-Portuguese Treaty of 11 June 1891 fixed the boundaries with Nyasaland and the BSAC territories; the Rovuma boundary and the occupation of the north (Niassa Company, to 1929) are not dated on the pages opened. The northern interior (Zambezia, Nampula, Cabo Delgado, Niassa) is a claim from 1891 and 1893 that was occupied only from 1900 and politically secured in 1918 ('secured political control over most of its territory in 1918'): its interior limit is soft until then.

notes: Cliopatria draws Mozambique only inside the Portuguese empire shapes (slug kingdom-of-portugal and the umbrella rel-portuguese-empire, other groups) and as 'Mozambique' from 1976; this dossier is the colony as its own state (type colony). Budget: seven pages (Portuguese Mozambique, Mutapa, Gaza, Gungunhana, the 1891 treaty, Mozambique Company, Niassa Company, Prazo); the prazo and company pages gave no territorial dates. Not entered as typed events because they change no sovereignty: the Mozambique Company (founded 11 February 1891, 'Manica and Sofala', 50-year concession, passed to the Portuguese authorities 18 July 1942), the Niassa Company (charter March 1893, Ruvuma to Lúrio, over 160,000 km2, extension refused 27 October 1929), the Zambezia prazos (no founding date on the Prazo page: 'known since the 16th century'; the Mutapa page: 1634 Tete prazos; in the 19th century 32 prazeiros owned 57 prazos in Tete Province). Not settled: when Portugal first held Sena and Quelimane (the Sena position is a gazetteer gap), the plateau feiras of the 1580s-1690s, the Manicaland claim (the 1891 treaty page: Manicaland 'passed from Portuguese to British control', undated before), the Rovuma boundary with German East Africa, the 1836-91 status name, the Pink Map (1885, 'Rose Coloured Map'). The Chioko rising is entered against 'mutapa-empire' although that dossier ends in 1885 (the infobox of the Mutapa page lists Chioko as 1890s-1902 ruler). Gazetteer names needed: place Sena (Mozambique, Zambezi), region Kionga Triangle (north bank of the Rovuma mouth, Cabo Delgado). The Kionga counterpart german-africa is a Cliopatria polity (af-08). REPAIR 2026-10-19 (after review): (1) K8 of the first version drew all of Mozambique in 1895 although only Tete (1885) and the Gaza provinces (1895) had events; the north is now entered as claims: Zambezia and Nampula in 1891 (the 11 June treaty; Nampula is a bridge), Cabo Delgado and Niassa in March 1893 (the Niassa Company charter), each from nobody, with keyframes portuguese-mozambique_1891 and _1893; effective occupation (1895-1902 Zambezi, 1900-1902 and 1909-1912 Niassa Company, 1918) is not dated as territory and is named in the notes and the certainty. Manica and Sofala, which the Mozambique Company held from 1891, come with the Gaza lands in 1895. (2) The 1632 valley gain is from nobody. (3) The Chioko contest and the war name 'Chioko's Mutapa-Barue coalition' as a string (a dossier for it is listed as a counterpart if the orchestrator wants one). (4) The Gaza overlap is settled in this dossier's favour: see K6. (5) The Sena page was opened for the thin item: no 1530s year; its coordinates (17.4417S 35.0272E) are for the gazetteer's Sena entry.
